soapandlyecontinued:basics-title: Soap and Lye: The Basics of Soap
soapandlyecontinued:basics-text:
Just Soap and Lye
Wood ash:
Your soap making journey begins with burning logs in a firepit to produce wood ash. It serves as the main ingredient for producing liquid lye.

Lye:
Liquid lye can be used in place of limewater for soaking animal hides or to make lye soap bars by mixing with fat in a barrel.

Soap bars:
The first soap bar you will make is a basic lye bar. This bar can then be immediately be combined in a barrel with water to make liquid lye soap or scented with honey.

Honey Soap:
Honey soap bars are worth the extra effort to produce as the liquid soap made from them requires less liters to wash items.

Liquid Soaps:
Liquid soap can be used to remove dye from cloth and leather, mordant from cloth, and to clean out dirty pots!

Potash:
Potash fertilizer can now be crafted by boiling water and wood ash in a cooking pot over a firepit!

Compatibility:

A Cullinary Artillery: Liquid soap can be bottled up and sold or purchased from various traders.

Food Shelves: Soap bars can be placed on the bar shelf!

Wildcraft Trees: Temporary conversion between charred logs and my wood ash until Wildcraft Trees is updated.

Wool: Liquid soap can be used to wash fleece and undye or remove mordant from all wool related items!
